dev.reply:
Yes
This rule is workable, unambiguous, and protects our core delivery rhythm. Hidden push refusals and unverified local commits derail TDD and slice workflows by letting us build on branch states that the remote rejected or hooks blocked. Verifying that the remote head matches the local commit and checking unpiped exit codes directly ensures that our incremental commit handoffs are honest and reproducible without requiring gaming or manual workarounds. The trial window and counter-metric properly protect against latency overhead.
CITE: every push writes its whole output and its own exit code to a file
